newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Industry Council to debate stricter state aid policy.
newsitem.headline: Industry Council to debate stricter state aid policy.

text.p: The Industry Council is industry expected to adopt on Thursday a Council resolution seeking more transparency and effectiveness in the control of state aid to ailing companies.

"The underlying aim is to make the control of state aid more effective, to make the application of rules more effective and transparent," one EU diplomat said. "It is really a design to bring transparancy, clarity and certainty of process into the way state aid is managed."

It was a "fairly modest" resolution which could encourage further proposals from the Commission, which is under increasing pressure from several smaller member states to clamp down on state aid, the diplomat added.

EU officials say the draft resolution has been largely agreed. However, a politically sensitive point is outstanding concerning the interaction between competition policy and other EU policies which aim at social and economic cohesion.
The resolution is based on an Irish presidency paper on state aid control which argues for more transparency in state aid, improvement of legal rules and lower state aid levels.

The Irish paper suggests that the Commission create a register or database to keep track of all state aid decisions and says the EU executive needs to have flexibility to focus on complex priority cases.
It points out that Europe cannot afford the present high levels of aid if it is remain competitive and reduce unemployment.
EU officials also say cutting aid would be in line with efforts to meet the criteria for monetary union.
The Irish initiative has won the support of DGIV (the directorate-general for competition policy), which faces an increasing workload, and the department has produced its own working paper.
DGIV argues for Commission proposals under treaty article 94, such as the the adoption of a regulation empowering the Commission to adopt legislation on exemptions from EU state aid rules.
Such legislation could exempt member states from the requirement to notify certain types of state aid, for example environment and research and development aid.

Article 94 says that the Council by a qualified majority "may make any appropriate regulations for the appliciation of articles 92 and 93 and may in particular determine the conditions in which article 93(3) shall apply and the categories of aid exempted from this procedure."
Articles 92 and 93 spell out the legal framework for EU state aid.

The Commission is under pressure to reduce government subsidies, a campaign led mainly by smaller EU states which, even if they wanted to, could not match the vast amounts of money being pumped into industries by the bloc's big countries, notably Germany and France.
The Commission said in its 1995 report on competition policy that the average annual aid for the Union as a whole was 94 billion European currency units, or 1.9 percent of EU gross domestic product.
The EU treaty bans any subsidies that distort fair competition, but leaves room for many exceptions.
The most common is rescue and restructuring aid if limited to bringing a firm back to profit.
